manifest.title: Noise and Recovery: Signal-to-Noise Challenge
manifest.subtitle: Controlled synthetic transit injection (depth 1,500 ppm) embedded in comparable photometric noise
preparationSteps: Injected 1,500 ppm periodic box signal at P = 4.120 days, epoch 52.30
Added 1,200 ppm Gaussian photometric noise to simulate high-precision space photometry

teaching.learningGoal: Understand how phase folding recovers shallow exoplanet signals buried in noise by stacking multiple transits.
guidedQuestions: In the raw time-series graph, can you spot the individual transits by eye?
Why does the transit dip become clearly visible once all 6 transits are folded together in the phase chart?
How does folding increase the signal-to-noise ratio?
teaching.explanationSummary: In the raw time series, a 1,500 ppm dip is almost invisible against 1,200 ppm random noise. But folding phase-aligns all 6 transits, reducing random noise by sqrt(N) and clearly revealing the shallow planet.

teacherAnswerReveal.astronomicalContext: Most Earth-sized and Neptune-sized planets are invisible in individual transits and require phase folding to detect.
teacherAnswerReveal.evidenceEvaluation: Shows 6 repeated transits with equal depths and no secondary eclipse. Recoverable with BLS search near P = 4.120 days.
alternativeExplanations: Instrumental red noise (eliminated by checking multi-event phase coherence).
